input: The seedbox rclone FUSE mount on the NAS died overnight and I remounted it. The mount looks healthy from the host now, but Sonarr still shows a health error like 'Deluge places downloads in /seedbox/tv ... but this directory does not exist', and inside the sonarr container 'ls /seedbox' says 'Socket not connected'. What's going on and what exactly do I need to do?
reference: The *arr fleet binds the rclone mount (/volume1/mounts/seedbox-files -> /seedbox) as PLAIN (non-propagating) bind mounts, so after any host-side remount every consumer container keeps the DEAD FUSE superblock ('Socket not connected') until it is restarted — a healthy host mount does not heal running containers. Fix: restart ALL /seedbox consumer containers, not just Sonarr: sonarr, radarr, lidarr, whisparr, bookshelf, unpackerr, mylar3. Use a full 'docker restart' — the in-app Restart on linuxserver containers can zombie (old process keeps the port, s6 spawns a new instance that crash-loops on 'address already in use'). The durable alternative is mount propagation: mark the mountpoint rshared (mount --make-rshared) and use :rslave binds (shelfmark does this and auto-recovers) — but a mid-life remount drops the rshared flag (it's only re-applied at boot), after which an rslave container fails to START ('not a shared or slave mount'); re-run make-rshared after any remount, then restart that container.

## Bitmagnet verification: what to probe, from where, and the pass line

The wiki identifies **three independent checks** — all three must pass. The service can return HTTP 200 on every probe and still be worthless, so each check probes a different layer of the stack.

### 1. DHT crawler is actually ingesting (`bitmagnet-dht-ingesting`)

**What this catches:** The crawler process is running but not discovering new torrents (UDP port 3334 blocked, Docker network issue, Postgres down). The HTTP server answers 200 but the index is a fossil.

**From where:** `mini` (the verification runner), SSH to `nas`

**The probe** (verbatim from `foss-setup/verification/checks.d/media-indexers.yaml`):
```bash
n=$(printf '%s\n' "$NAS_SUDO_PASSWORD" | ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 nas \
  "sudo -S -p '' /usr/local/bin/docker exec bitmagnet-postgres psql -U postgres -d bitmagnet \
   -tAc \"SELECT count(*) FROM torrents WHERE created_at > now() - interval '30 minutes'\"" \
  2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
{ [ -n "$n" ] && [ "$n" -gt 0 ] && echo "ingesting=yes recent30m=$n"; } \
  || echo "ingesting=NO recent30m=${n:-query_failed}"
```

**Pass line:** Output matches `^ingesting=yes recent30m=[1-9][0-9]*$` — at least one new torrent row in the last 30 minutes.

**If it fails:** Check crawler logs (`sudo /usr/local/bin/docker logs --tail 30 bitmagnet` for `started worker {"key": "dht_crawler"}`), confirm `3334/udp` is published in `docker ps`, verify Postgres is running.

---

### 2. Torznab endpoint is usable from the consumer (`bitmagnet-torznab-via-prowlarr`)

**What this catches:** The endpoint can serve 200s while being functionally useless. This is the **consumer-end probe** — it runs from `mini`, hits Prowlarr on the `nas`, and performs an actual Torznab search against bitmagnet's registered indexer.

**From where:** `mini`

```

**What this catches:** Bitmagnet's Prowlarr Sync Profile got flipped back to `Standard`, re-enabling RSS and automatic search — causing the arrs to auto-grab junk (foreign dubs, re-encodes) that the DHT crawler has classified.

# 3. Raw Torznab bypass (no classification layer) — immediate result but low-signal:
curl -s 'http://192.168.10.4:3333/torznab/api?t=search&q=1080p' | grep -c '<item>'
```

reference: Root cause: Bazarr has ZERO subtitle providers enabled — /api/system/settings shows general.enabled_providers=[] and /api/providers returns {'data': []}. This is a regression of done work media-12 (2026-07-28), whose deploy-time state had Podnapisi as the sole enabled provider (proven then with 27 real candidates); the provider config has since been removed/lost — on-disk /volume1/docker/bazarr/config/config/config.yaml line 'enabled_providers: []' confirms it's persisted state, not an API quirk. With no providers, nothing in the wanted backlog can EVER be fetched. Monitoring stays green because bazarr-synced-from-arrs by design only asserts the arr->Bazarr sync side (movie/series counts + arr connectivity), never the provider/consumer end — textbook green-but-broken. Config-only confirmation (no searches): (1) GET /api/system/settings -> enabled_providers []; (2) GET /api/providers -> empty data; (3) GET /api/episodes/history and /api/movies/history -> total=0 (no subtitle ever downloaded); (4) read the on-disk config.yaml. Fix direction: re-enable Podnapisi (optionally add an OpenSubtitles account per the check's own handoff note) and add a cheap provider-count assertion (enabled_providers non-empty via the settings API — rate-limit safe) so this class alerts.

checklist.desc: Identifies the root cause: no subtitle providers enabled at all (enabled_providers empty) — a lost/removed provider config regression, so the fetch side is completely dead
Explains why the check stays green: bazarr-synced-from-arrs only asserts arr↔Bazarr sync/counts, not provider config or actual subtitle downloads (green-but-broken / consumer-end gap)
Gives config-only confirmation probes that trigger no provider search: settings API enabled_providers, /api/providers, download history totals=0, and/or the on-disk config.yaml
Does not attribute the backlog to arr sync problems, indexers, or Bazarr being down — sync and liveness are demonstrably fine
Fix direction: re-enable a provider (Podnapisi was the deploy-time provider) and/or add a provider-count assertion to monitoring

## Root Cause: Language profile not assigned to pre-existing media

From **kb/wiki/services/bazarr.md** (line 33):

> **Bazarr shows a series/movie but never searches subtitles for it** — A language profile only auto-applies to media ADDED after it existed; pre-existing items sync from the arrs with NO profile and are inert.

Bazarr synced all 2868 episodes + 27 movies from Sonarr/Radarr, but because those items were pre-existing in the arrs, Bazarr assigned them NO language profile. An item with no profile is inert — Bazarr will never search for, download, or log anything in history for it. The history is empty because zero searches were ever initiated.

The enabled providers (gestdown for TV, yifysubtitles for movies — per kb/wiki/services/bazarr.md) are irrelevant here: the providers are never called because the items never reach the search stage.

## Why `bazarr-synced-from-arrs` stays green

The check (kb/wiki/reference/checks/media-subtitles.md, line 13) runs:

```python
b = g('/api/badges')                          # SignalR status
m = g('/api/movies?length=1')                 # Movie count
s = g('/api/series?length=1')                 # Series count
ok = (b.get('sonarr_signalr') == 'LIVE'
   and b.get('radarr_signalr') == 'LIVE'
   and m.get('total', 0) > 0)                 # movies > 0 only
```

It prints `BAZARR_OK movies=%d series=%d sonarr=%s radarr=%s` — the output string includes both movie and series counts, but the `ok` condition only validates **three things**:
1. `sonarr_signalr == 'LIVE'`
2. `radarr_signalr == 'LIVE'`
3. `movies.total > 0`

It does **not** validate `series.total > 0`, `missing_subtitles`, download history, or provider health. All three conditions are trivially true: SignalR links are live and the movie count is non-zero. The check confirms Bazarr is connected and has media in its library — it does not confirm that subtitle downloads are happening.

The complementary check `bazarr-providers-can-fetch` (line 24) **would** catch this: it verifies `fetched >= 1` by summing episode and movie history totals. With an empty history, this check would fail.

import json,sys
d = json.load(sys.stdin)
if d:
    print('Sample series:', d[0]['title'], 'missing_subtitles:', d[0].get('missing_subtitles', 0))
print('Total series in Bazarr:', d.get('total', 0))
"

curl -s "http://192.168.10.4:6767/api/movies?length=1" | python3 -c "
import json,sys
d = json.load(sys.stdin)
if d:
    print('Sample movie:', d[0]['title'], 'missing_subtitles:', d[0].get('missing_subtitles', 0))
print('Total movies in Bazarr:', d.get('total', 0))
"

# 2. Confirm history is empty (read-only)

curl -s "http://192.168.10.4:6767/api/movies/history?start=0&length=1" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('Movie history total:', d.get('total',0))"

# 3. Confirm the English profile (id=1) exists on Bazarr

"
```

- **`missing_subtitles` is populated for the sample items** — the items are seen as having missing subtitles

Per the wiki (kb/wiki/services/bazarr.md line 33), assign the English profile (id 1) in bulk:

**For movies** (exact API from the wiki):
```bash
curl -s "http://192.168.10.4:6767/api/movies" | python3 -c "
import json,sys
for m in json.load(sys.stdin):
    print(m['radarrid'])
" | while read radarrid; do
    curl -s "http://192.168.10.4:6767/api/movies?radarrid=$radarrid&profileid=1"
done
```

```bash
curl -s "http://192.168.10.4:6767/api/series" | python3 -c "

for s in json.load(sys.stdin):
    print(s['tvdbid'])
" | while read tvdbid; do
    curl -s "http://192.168.10.4:6767/api/series?tvdbid=$tvdbid&profileid=1"
done
```

After assigning profiles, trigger a disk scan (per wiki: `PATCH /api/movies` with `action=scan-disk` for movies, or the equivalent series scan) so Bazarr recomputes `missing_subtitles` for the now-profiled items. The scheduled search will then begin downloading subtitles and the history will populate.

---

**Summary:** The root cause is the language-profile gap for pre-existing media. The monitoring stays green because `bazarr-synced-from-arrs` only checks SignalR connectivity and library counts — it never inspects subtitle download activity. The fix is bulk-assigning the English profile to all existing series and movies, then triggering a disk scan.

The `llm-triage.sh` script defaults to the rig's llama-swap endpoint (`:9292/v1`, model `qwen3.6-35b-a3b`) which is healthy. However, the script **sources** `/etc/verification/env` before making requests (`set -a; . env`). A stale `LLM_BASE_URL=http://rig:11434` override — left over from the old Ollama era — would redirect every request to the **ollama compat shim**, which is exactly the mechanism documented in `kb/wiki/runbooks/verification-self.md`:

> the ollama `:11434` shim answers `/models` 200 but 404s a big-model completion, which is exactly how the failure hid for days

This explains every symptom:

| Symptom | Why |
|---|---|
| `HTTP Error 404: Not Found` in triage stubs | If the override redirects to :11434, a POST for `qwen3.6-35b-a3b` hits the shim, which only holds `nomic-embed-text`, `tag:fast`, `llama3.2:3b` — the model is unknown → 404 |
| `llm_up()` gate never trips | The gate probes `/v1/models` which returns HTTP 200 from the shim (liveness passes), so WoL is never triggered |
| Script in the repo looks correct | The repo default is right; the override lives in the runtime env file on mini, not in the script |
| No incident alert fires | `llm_up()` returning 200 means the rig is "up" from the gate's perspective |

The `llm-triage-completion-e2e` self-check (`/opt/verification/bin/llm-triage-probe.sh`) is designed to catch exactly this scenario.

The Healthchecks dead-man (`verification-mini`) is healthy because the verification service carries `SuccessExitStatus=1` — a failing check (exit 1) is treated as success, so the dead-man ping fires regardless of check outcomes.

**Step 2 — Re-probe the triage path directly:**
```bash

```

```bash

```bash
ssh mini '/opt/verification/bin/verify-cycle.sh'
```

The wiki documents three triage failure modes for this check:

- **`http_404` / `http_5xx`** — wrong endpoint or model (the env override scenario above)
- **`empty_content`** — the model returned 200 but no content (reasoning models like `qwen3.6` spend `max_tokens` on hidden thinking; if the probe's budget is too small, the answer is empty)
- **`curl_error`** — the rig is unreachable (not the case here; both endpoints responded 200)

If Step 1 shows no override, the `empty_content` path is the next suspect — the reasoning model may be returning a valid response with an empty content field, which the triage parser treats as a failure.

### Bottom line

The rig's llama-swap is healthy right now (confirmed). The most likely root cause is a stale `LLM_BASE_URL` override in `/etc/verification/env` on mini redirecting requests to the ollama shim. Run Step 1 to confirm or rule it out.

### The root cause: monitoring gap + check logic bug

The user reports the "Bazarr monitoring check is green" while the enabled-providers list is empty. Two checks exist for Bazarr (per `kb/wiki/reference/checks/media-subtitles.md`):

**`bazarr-synced-from-arrs`** (primary liveness check) verifies:
1. `sonarr_signalr == "LIVE"` — SignalR connection to Sonarr
2. `radarr_signalr == "LIVE"` — SignalR connection to Radarr
3. `movies.total > 0` — library sync worked

This check **does not verify providers**. It will stay green as long as Bazarr can reach Sonarr and Radarr and has a non-zero movie count — completely independent of whether subtitle providers are configured.

**`bazarr-providers-can-fetch`** (consumer-end check, fix-59) is supposed to verify providers, but **it has a logic bug**:

The check's bash command queries:
```
fetched=g('/api/episodes/history?start=0&length=1').get('total',0)+g('/api/movies/history?start=0&length=1').get('total',0)
ok=(len(ep)>=1 and len(good)>=1 and fetched>=1)
```

The `fetched` field is the **total count of historical subtitle fetches** (from `/api/episodes/history` and `/api/movies/history`). With a ~2,900 episode backlog and ~29 movie backlog, if Bazarr has ever fetched subtitles, `fetched` will be a large number and `fetched>=1` will pass. **The check requires `fetched>=1` (at least one subtitle ever fetched), not `fetched>0 since last check` or any recency constraint.** Combined with the `providers>=1` and `good>=1` checks, if providers were wiped, this check *should* fail. But the healthchecks summary shows 0 not-up, meaning this check is either not deployed to `/opt/verification/checks.d/`, not enabled, or not running.

The verification ran today (journal shows `353/376 passed, 23 failed`) and neither bazarr check appeared in the failure list. The KB wiki says checks run "hourly/daily by the verification harness" but doesn't specify which is which, and I cannot confirm this check is actually deployed and enabled on this fleet.

The KB wiki (`kb/wiki/services/bazarr.md`) documents that in fix-59 (2026-08-03), the original provider **Podnapisi was removed from Bazarr upstream** in v1.6.0 — the provider module was gone and the config migration had to handle this. The current providers are **gestdown** (Addic7ed API) for TV and **yifysubtitles** for movies, both free with no account required.

The user states the providers list is now empty and "nothing obvious in our configs changed." I cannot determine the mechanism from the available evidence — whether it was a config migration edge case, a Docker restart, or something else. The NAS is under heavy I/O load per the user, but I cannot prove that caused the provider wipe.

## How to restore subtitle fetching

### Step 1: Probe the live API state

From the mini host (where the `BAZARR_API_KEY` environment variable is set by the verification harness):

```bash
# Check enabled providers in settings
curl -s http://192.168.10.4:6767/api/system/settings \
  -H "X-API-KEY: $BAZARR_API_KEY" | python3 -m json.tool

# Check provider statuses
curl -s http://192.168.10.4:6767/api/providers \
  -H "X-API-KEY: $BAZARR_API_KEY" | python3 -m json.tool

# Check subtitle history totals
curl -s http://192.168.10.4:6767/api/episodes/history?start=0\&length=1 \
  -H "X-API-KEY: $BAZARR_API_KEY" | python3 -m json.tool
curl -s http://192.168.10.4:6767/api/movies/history?start=0\&length=1 \
  -H "X-API-KEY: $BAZARR_API_KEY" | python3 -m json.tool
```

This will confirm: which providers are enabled, their health status, and whether any subtitles have been fetched historically.

### Step 2: Re-enable providers

Per the KB wiki, the two working providers are:
- **gestdown** — Addic7ed API (free, no account) for TV episodes
- **yifysubtitles** (free, no account) for movies

**Via the Bazarr UI:** Settings → Providers → enable gestdown and yifysubtitles.

The exact API calls to re-enable providers depend on the Bazarr REST API format (which is not documented in the KB), so the UI is the safest path. After enabling, Bazarr should automatically begin searching the backlog.

### Step 3: Trigger the backlog search

**Via the Bazarr UI:** Settings → General → ensure scheduled search is enabled, or manually trigger a search for missing subtitles.

**Via the API** (after confirming the endpoint format from the Bazarr docs at `docs.linuxserver.io/images/docker-bazarr/`):

```

```bash
ssh nas 'find /volume3/tv -name "*.srt" -type f 2>/dev/null | head -10'
ssh nas 'find /volume2/movies -name "*.srt" -type f 2>/dev/null | head -10'

### The gap identified

1. **`bazarr-synced-from-arrs` is a liveness check, not a health check.** It confirms Bazarr can reach the arrs but says nothing about provider configuration or subtitle fetching capability.

2. **`bazarr-providers-can-fetch` has a recency bug.** The `fetched>=1` check uses total historical fetch count, not recent fetches. With a large backlog, this will always pass once Bazarr has fetched at least one subtitle in its lifetime. It should check for fetches within a reasonable window (e.g., last 24 hours) rather than total count.

3. **Neither check may be deployed.** The verification results today showed 353/376 passed with no bazarr checks in the failure list. The check files were not found on the filesystem (`/opt/verification/checks.d/` is not accessible via glob). ## Corrected final answer

### The resolver chain

DHCP on every client VLAN is intended to hand out **three** DNS servers, in this order:

| # | IP | Host | What it is | Upstream |
|---|-----|------|------------|----------|
| **1** | `192.168.10.2` | mini | AdGuard Home (primary) → **Unbound** (recursive + DNSSEC) | Unbound on mini (root hints + DNSSEC) over the shared Docker `edge` network (`unbound:5335`) |
| **2** | `192.168.10.4` | NAS | AdGuard Home (secondary) | Public Quad9 DoH (`https://dns10.quad9.net/dns-query`); the troubleshooting guidance also recommends adding `tls://1.1.1.1` and `tls://9.9.9.9` as additional upstreams |
| **3** | `192.168.10.1` | UniFi gateway | Bare internet DNS (ISP resolvers) | ISP DNS — no filtering, no local names |

Both AdGuard instances carry **DNS rewrites**: every `*.tabaska.us` name is rewritten to `192.168.10.2` (the mini's LAN IP). There is no public Cloudflare record for `*.tabaska.us`; it is internal-only by construction. The Caddy reverse proxy on the mini serves the `*.tabaska.us` vhosts.

#### Upstream detail for hop 1

AdGuard on the mini doesn't talk to the internet directly. Its upstream is the sibling **Unbound** container (`adguard/adguardhome:v0.107.77` → `unbound:5335` over the Docker `edge` network). Inside the AdGuard container, `127.0.0.1:5335` would be AdGuard's own loopback — the config must use `unbound:5335` (the Docker network alias).

#### Upstream detail for hop 2

The NAS AdGuard uses **public Quad9 DoH** (`https://dns10.quad9.net/dns-query`), deliberately *not* mini Unbound, so it can resolve external names independently when the mini is offline. The troubleshooting guidance also recommends adding `tls://1.1.1.1` and `tls://9.9.9.9` as additional upstreams so one flaky provider doesn't stall lookups.

### What happens when the mini goes down

The specific symptom: *"wiki.tabaska.us and every other `*.tabaska.us` site dead while Google still works and DNS lookups for those names still succeed."*

1. **DNS lookups succeed** — the NAS AdGuard (hop 2) is still running and still has the `*.tabaska.us → 192.168.10.2` rewrite. A `dig @192.168.10.4 wiki.tabaska.us` returns `192.168.10.2`.

2. **The HTTP request fails** — because the rewrite points to `192.168.10.2` (the mini), and the Caddy reverse proxy on the mini (which serves the `*.tabaska.us` vhosts) is down. The IP resolves, but nothing is listening on port 443 at that address.

3. **Google still works** — because the NAS AdGuard's upstream (Quad9 DoH) is independent of the mini.

This is a **proxy/application outage**, not a DNS outage. The DNS layer is working correctly; the application layer at `192.168.10.2` is gone.

| Query | Path | Result when mini is down |
|-------|------|--------------------------|
| `dig wiki.tabaska.us` | Client → hop 1 (dead) → **hop 2** (NAS AdGuard, alive) → rewrite returns `192.168.10.2` | ✅ Resolves |
| `dig google.com` | Client → hop 1 (dead) → **hop 2** (NAS AdGuard) → Quad9 DoH upstream | ✅ Resolves |
| `GET https://wiki.tabaska.us` | Browser → DNS → `192.168.10.2:443` → **Caddy on mini is dead** | ❌ Connection refused |

### Current state of the architecture

- **dns-01** (mini: Unbound + AdGuard + rewrites) — **done**
- **dns-02** (NAS secondary AdGuard + mirrored rewrites/blocklists) — **done** (validated 2026-07-14). The NAS container runs `network_mode: host` (since fix-40, 2026-07-19) so real client IPs reach AdGuard for per-client stats and querylog forensics.
- **dns-03** (UniFi DHCP fail-open chain on all client VLANs) — **open**. Until this is done, a client on a VLAN not yet configured with the three-server chain may sit on a single dead resolver.
- **dns-04** (verify script + outage runbook) — **done**. The script lives at `scripts/network/dns-resilience-verify.sh`.
- **dns-05** (NAT `:53` redirect + DoH blocking) — **deferred**. Enabling it before dns-03 would recreate the single-point-of-failure.

The verification sweep probes both resolvers hourly/daily with auto-reopen on regression. The scripted outage drill (dns-04) has never been run end-to-end.

### Verification commands (from any LAN machine)

```bash
# Hop 1 — mini AdGuard: external name + local rewrite
dig @192.168.10.2 example.com +time=2 +tries=1
dig @192.168.10.2 wiki.tabaska.us +short        # expect 192.168.10.2

# Hop 2 — NAS AdGuard: must work with the mini DOWN
dig @192.168.10.4 example.com +time=2 +tries=1
dig @192.168.10.4 wiki.tabaska.us +short        # expect 192.168.10.2

# Hop 3 — gateway: external only (no local names expected)
dig @192.168.10.1 example.com +time=2 +tries=1

# What is DHCP actually handing out? (macOS)
ipconfig getpacket en0 | grep domain_name_server
# expect: {192.168.10.2, 192.168.10.4, 192.168.10.1}
```

Scripted verification: `bash foss-setup/scripts/network/dns-resilience-verify.sh`

### Diagnosis quick-reference

| Finding | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Hop 1 dead, hop 2 answers | mini down/rebooting — **expected, self-heals** | Wait or fix the mini; clients ride hop 2 |
| Hop 1 dead, hop 2 dead | NAS AdGuard container not running | DSM → Container Manager → project `adguard-nas` → Start |
| Hop 1 up but external names fail | Unbound broken behind AdGuard | `ssh mini 'cd /opt/stacks/unbound && docker compose logs --tail 50'`; restart the unbound stack |
| Local names fail only on hop 2 | Rewrites not mirrored to NAS AdGuard | Re-import rewrites/blocklists from the mini instance (dns-02) |
| DHCP handout wrong | Out-of-band UniFi change | **Human, GUI**: Settings → Networks → each VLAN → DHCP DNS = `10.2, 10.4, 10.1` exactly |
